Verified empirically: GET /momento/../admin/secret with momento_url=https://host/base/ is sent upstream as /base/../admin/secret, which any normal upstream normalises to /admin/secret. The docs (admin-guide.md 'forwards /momento/* to <momento_url>/*') and the comment promise base-path confinement, but an anonymous user can reach any path on the collector host. On a transient read failure the handler then persists only the new origin, silently wiping the existing tracking.allowed_hosts list; the 'no tracking on outage' fallback is right for page rendering but wrong for a write path. Two concurrent allow clicks also lose one update (no version check). / internal/httpapi/settings_handlers.go:137 tracking.allowed_hosts is validated only by stringLimit(4096); every whitespace/comma token is spliced verbatim into script-src/connect-src/img-src (tracking.go:250-254). A value such as 'unsafe-inline' or * is accepted and shipped in the header, contradicting the commit message, the UI copy and admin-guide.md ('never widened with unsafe-inline'). handleAllowTrackingHost validates origins but the ordinary PUT /admin/settings path does not.

internal/httpapi/tracking_handlers.go:389-399 handleAllowTrackingHost does a read-modify-write with s.trackingConfig(), which deliberately swallows SettingsMap errors and returns Config{} (AllowedHosts=""). On a transient read failure the handler then persists only the new origin, silently wiping the existing tracking.allowed_hosts list; the 'no tracking on outage' fallback is right for page rendering but wrong for a write path. notes: Build, go vet, go test ./internal/tracking ./internal/httpapi, web tsc -b and vitest AdminPages.test.ts all pass; embedded dist bundle references the new /admin/tracking API so the rebuild is consistent with source.

tracking_handlers.go:230-232 and admin-guide.md say CSP reports are 'kept in memory, never in the database', but the route sits under /api/v1 which carries requestAudit, so every browser report (unauthenticated, no rate limiter unlike /auth/login) inserts a row into api_request_logs. Not the report body, but it is unbounded DB write volume driven by anonymous clients.

Anyone can POST fabricated csp-report bodies: 100-entry recorder can be flushed of real entries, and attacker-chosen origins appear in the admin table with a one-click '허용' button (social-engineering path into script-src). Document-uri is shown via React so no XSS.
Config.Active excludes /admin only by exact/prefix case-sensitive match while React Router matches routes case-insensitively, so /ADMIN/... receives the snippet with include_admin=false. Minor.

/momento (no trailing slash) is not matched by the '/momento/*' route and falls through to the SPA handler, but isDocumentPath treats it as non-document so it serves index.html with default-src 'none'. Harmless but inconsistent.

tracking.custom_snippet lets any settings.write principal inject arbitrary script into every user's page including /login (docs acknowledge this). This is inherent to the feature, but it materially raises what settings.write grants; worth calling out in the permission docs.

Tests are meaningful: nonce count/uniqueness, policy directives, credential stripping, recorder eviction and the ASCII-fold index regression are all asserted against the real code. Vite hash renames in internal/webui/dist are a side effect of the rebuild, not scope creep. No migrations; revert is clean (settings rows for tracking.* would remain but are ignored).
